verdict.label: separate
verdict.why: Both functions build an Atom.family keyed by a JSON-encoded target, call createUrl, and wrap the query in Atom.transform with initialValueTarget, a subscribe-and-setSelf pattern, and setIdleTTL(0). That is shared scaffolding over the same Effect Atom API, not a shared domain operation. The decision logic inside the transform differs. NEW tracks per-registry minted revisions, refreshes once on a revision change, and keeps the previous shown value stable via keepUnchangedFile. EXISTING refreshes when a URL's remaining life falls below minLifeMs, and hides the expiring URL by returning an initial(true) result. The triggers, state, and outputs are different, so there is no common reusable policy. Pulling out the family/transform wrapper would be a generic helper with little contract, and the two callers would still need to pass nearly all of their behavior in as callbacks.
